title: Operating Systems
description: Complete 21-Module Master Operating Systems & Linux Internals Reference Guide covering Fundamentals, Kernel, Processes, Threads, CPU Scheduling, IPC, Synchronization, Memory, Virtual Memory, File Systems, Storage, I/O, Networking, Security, Virtualization, Containers, Linux Internals, Performance, Real-World Applications, Practical Linux CLI, and Interview & System Design.
learning_objectives: Understand OS kernel architectures (Monolithic, Microkernel, Hybrid)
Master boot process, system calls, interrupt handling, and user vs kernel mode
Understand process virtual address spaces, process creation (fork/exec), and context switching
Master thread execution models, synchronization primitives (Mutex, Semaphore, Monitors), and Deadlocks
Master CPU scheduling algorithms (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, MLFQ) and real-time scheduling
Understand memory management, paging, TLB, multi-level page tables, and demand paging
Master Unix File Systems, Inodes, File Descriptors, VFS, and Page Cache
Understand Linux Containers, Namespaces (PID/Net/Mount), Cgroups, and Virtualization
Master networking sockets, I/O multiplexing (select, poll, epoll), and event-driven architectures
Diagnose production performance using Linux CLI tools (top, htop, vmstat, iostat, lsof, strace)
